key_insight: CARM improves response-level off-policy control in LLM reinforcement learning by masking whole samples using the average absolute token log-ratio, so opposing probability shifts cannot cancel out.
engineering_relevance: It gives practitioners a more robust sequence-level acceptance rule for RL post-training pipelines where rollout and training engines differ, helping reduce harmful off-policy updates in reasoning and code models.
method: Compute token log-ratios between sampled rollout probabilities and training-engine probabilities.
Use the mean absolute log-ratio across the sequence instead of the signed geometric mean to avoid cancellation.
Accept only responses that satisfy a joint bound on out-of-band token ratios and mean log-distance beyond the band.
evidence_signal: On mathematical reasoning and code generation benchmarks, CARM improved mean@16 on AIME 2024/2025/2026 plus BeyondAIME by up to 3.13 points, and raised average pass@1 on four code benchmarks by 2.88 points over the strongest baseline.
watch_item: Because masking is stricter and sequence-level, the method may reduce usable samples or require careful tuning of the ratio band and acceptance threshold.
paper_title: CARM: Cancellation-Aware Response Masking for LLM Reinforcement Learning
